# Minimum Moves to Convert String. 'O' is the capital letter O.

@example One stamp on positions 1 to 3 and another on 4 to 6.
"OXOOXXO"
=> 2

@example The 'X's at 0 and 2 share the stamp on 0 to 2; the last 'X' needs its own, on 5 to 7.
"XOXOOOOX"
=> 2

@example The 'X's are three places apart, so no stamp covers two of them.
"XOOXOOX"
=> 3

# The shortest string, with no 'X'.
"OOO"
=> 0

# Three characters: any 'X' needs exactly one stamp.
"OOX"
=> 1

"XOX"
=> 1

# A single 'X' in the last place, and two in the last two places.
"OOOOOX"
=> 1

"XOOOXX"
=> 2

# Three runs of 'X', yet two stamps do.
"XOXOX"
=> 2

# Four 'X's, but each needs its own stamp: not 4 / 3 rounded up.
"XOOXOOXOOX"
=> 4

# 'X's two apart share stamps.
"OXOXOXOX"
=> 2

# Four 'X's in a row need two stamps, seven need three.
"OXXXXO"
=> 2

"XXXXXXX"
=> 3

# 1000 characters, all 'X': 334 stamps.
""
=> 334

# An 'X' at every third place from the first: 334 stamps.
""
=> 334

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 2 small
"XXOOXXO"
=> 2

@gen 3 small
"XXXXXXXXOXOXOX"
=> 5

@gen 7 small
"OOOOXOXOOOXO"
=> 2

@gen 11 small
"OOXXOOXOOOXXO"
=> 3

@gen 12 small
"XOOXXOXXXO"
=> 3

@gen 19 small
"OXOXOOOOXOOXO"
=> 3

@gen 20 small
"OXXOXOXOX"
=> 3

@gen 28 small
"XXXXOXOOXOOXX"
=> 4

# Full size: 'X's spread out, always in the last two places; all 'O'
# but the last character; random.
@gen 3
""
=> 140

@gen 4
""
=> 1

@gen 5
""
=> 321
